repair_contract.wait_callback: When state.wait_observer exists, preserve its original invocation on every original event with unmodified frame,event,arg; never filter away c_call/c_return/lock events or alter ordering. It may perform its original work. Lifecycle sampling must not change its exception semantics.
selected_boundaries: Actual real_poll call/return: preserve entered/thread/sequence observations; original wrapper finally sampling remains.

repair_contract.association: Use exact session.worker and registered session/worker/thread object identities. No names-only ownership. Permit explicit session argument/private association helper when worker session field is not yet installed; do not mutate product fields. Avoid scanning all workers on ordinary events. Lifecycle-only bounded scans are allowed; a thread-to-owner map is preferable once identity is known.
repair_contract.actual_peaks: Retain observed peak semantics and original cap checks. Thread start/close and concurrent identities must support observed counts; never label missing observations as zero or assert an exact OS-wide peak. Every allocated resource retains original denominator and cleanup.
repair_contract.instrumentation: Permit bounded aggregate sample/lifecycle counts in the resource observations and a test-only metric accessor; increment only at actual sampling/boundaries, no per-profile-event lists/counters. Ordinary unrelated CPU event burst must add zero runtime samples.
repair_contract.restoration: Same original sys/thread profile and trace identities restored in finally; no extra sampler thread, sleep, yield/GIL tuning or forced scheduling.
